name: Tour de l'Échangeur de Limete
region: Kinshasa · Democratic Republic of the Congo
subtitle: Monumental 210-metre brutalist concrete tower and Patrice Lumumba mausoleum defining Kinshasa's skyline.

facts.label: Architect & era
facts.value: Olivier-Clément Cacoub (constructed 1970–1974 under Mobutu Sese Seko)

facts.label: National memorial
facts.value: Mausoleum and bronze statue honoring national hero and first Prime Minister Patrice Émery Lumumba

parts.text: The defining architectural landmark and skyline silhouette of Kinshasa, situated at the major highway junction in Limete. Commissioned in the early 1970s under President Mobutu Sese Seko and designed by French-Tunisian architect Olivier-Clément Cacoub, this monumental reinforced-concrete tower rises 210 meters above the metropolis with four fluted pillars. The surrounding esplanade houses the national memorial and mausoleum dedicated to Patrice Émery Lumumba, hero of Congolese independence.
